facts.claim: The company manufactures sterile liquid parenterals at Hariyala/Kheda, Gujarat, and sells domestic brands, exports, and contract-manufactures for third parties. FY26 line configuration was four LVP and three SVP lines.
Portfolio includes large-volume IV fluids, electrolytes, anti-infectives, SVP injections/diluents, ophthalmic, irrigation and respiratory/nebulization products; fill volumes span 2-1,000 ml.

FY26 reported installed capacity was 5.7 crore LVP units excluding SteriPort, 20.9 crore SVP units and 6.6 crore SteriPort bottles; FY26 utilization LVP 93%, SVP 98%, SteriPort 90%. Chart history FY23-26: LVP 97/93/91/93%, SVP 89/94/99/98%, SteriPort 73/83/91/90%. Nearby prose cites overall/current utilization of 96% without defining calculation.

SteriPort uses ISBM / RCPP two-port packaging; management says it lowers contamination risk, improves container integrity and is compatible with potent oncology/critical-care drugs; claimed ~42% FY26 operating revenue contribution.

Company presents sterile manufacturing as capital-, energy- and compliance-intensive and says its three-decade experience and certifications create barriers to entry; report does not quantify market share, relative cost, yields, customer retention or switching costs.

FY26 export presence was 20 countries; 47 products were registered in 120 jurisdictions; domestic network ~320 distributors/stockists and ~96 sales/marketing personnel. Geographic revenue: India ₹17,349.76 lakh; outside India ₹11,069.63 lakh. No customer/group contributed >=10% of revenue.

IPO fresh issue: 1 crore shares at ₹126, ₹12,600 lakh gross proceeds; net proceeds ₹10,315.19 lakh after ₹2,284.81 lakh issue expenses. FY26-end unused ₹5,246.75 lakh; prospectus targeted ₹8,000 lakh utilization by FY26. Auditor notes delay vs timeline; proceeds held in fixed deposits / monitoring account.

CRISIL monitoring report says cumulative issue-object spend reached ₹7,495.43 lakh by 30 Sep 2026, from ₹4,766.36 lakh at FY26 close; delay persisted due to payment timing based on work/supply completion and machinery-order terms. Deviation from objects: not applicable. CRISIL says it does not audit or independently verify issuer information.
FY26 report describes approx ₹90 crore SteriPort and ₹30.13 crore SVP lines; targets SteriPort capacity expansion from 6.6 to ~12 crore bottles/year and a ~20-product pipeline.
Company announced production commencement at new Kheda SteriPort facility on 2 Sep 2026; report's earlier target had been September 2026.
FY26 report gives 10.8 MW plant capex ₹3,480 lakh, ₹580 lakh company outlay, balance term-loan funded; projected ₹900 lakh annual savings and 3.6-year pre-interest payback.
Company announced captive solar plant commissioned and generation started 30 May 2026; announcement confirms start but not achieved savings.
FY26 contingent legal disputes ₹1,698.78 lakh: GST ₹1,659.08 lakh, income tax ₹11.18 lakh, DPCO ₹28.52 lakh. GST relates mainly to input tax credit issues.
Advance License Scheme incremental export obligation US$41.40 lakh / ₹3,691.95 lakh; unprovided potential customs duty if unfulfilled ₹713.92 lakh, vs ₹3.06 lakh prior year.
PPE capital commitments not provided for: ₹1,880.26 lakh at FY26 end.
Price Waterhouse Chartered Accountants LLP issued unmodified opinion; provisions/contingent liabilities were key audit matter. Company reports auditor no-resignation during FY26.
Audit trail/edit log operated in accounting software; database layer not independently verified; auditor reports no tampering observed.

FY26 RPTs: CMD short-term benefits ₹108 lakh; CFO Paras Mehta benefits ₹85.03 lakh; land purchase from CMD ₹102.46 lakh; vehicle lease rent ₹28.80 lakh; ₹11.91 lakh CSR expense with Health and Care Foundation (CMD is trustee). Year-end payable CMD ₹4.44 lakh and Paras Mehta ₹8.34 lakh.
AGM disclosure identifies Nimesh Patel as cousin of CMD Bhavesh Patel.

CMD FY26 remuneration ₹120 lakh (salary/allowances ₹108 lakh, perquisites ₹3 lakh, PF ₹9 lakh); proposed monthly pay ₹13.29 lakh effective 1 Apr 2026 vs ₹10 lakh previously, subject to AGM approval; September AGM announcement confirms approval.

facts.claim: COO Anil Rathi resignation effective 29 Oct 2026, reason cited as better opportunity and growth.
CRISIL upgraded ₹245 crore bank facilities to BBB/Stable and A3+ from BBB-/Stable and A3 in February 2026. Rating rationale also identifies competition and packing-material cost volatility.

Expansion execution and utilization, sterile-quality/regulatory compliance, GST disputes and export-duty obligation, input-cost volatility, audit-trail controls, and related-party transaction oversight are material monitoring areas. Solar cost savings are projected, not yet evidenced in this annual report.
